admitted.text: Pace seems to value consent as an active choice that must remain available even inside surrender.
admitted.detail_quote: that was what he did, he backed off and let her decide

admitted.text: Pace reads as patient and courtly, repeatedly leaving the decisive last movement to Vee.
admitted.detail_quote: He stood in the shadow with her and left the last inch where it was.

admitted.text: Pace seems deeply gratified by bringing hidden wants into view, which makes his care inseparable from an appetite for revelation.
admitted.detail_quote: the voice of a woman who was not performing because she had run out of the apparatus of performance.

admitted.text: Pace reads as extraordinarily observant, noticing appetites and discomforts other people overlook.
admitted.detail_quote: he had laid the slices in the bowl with the cut sides up because he had noticed that she ate them faster when the cut sides showed

admitted.text: His restraint seems to come from an old wound, a lesson he learned about respecting a closed door.
admitted.detail_quote: A closed door was hers, not his; you did not open it just because you could hear through it.

admitted.text: He seems to be quietly guarding something of Vee's from Randi, which hints at a real attachment growing outside the game.
admitted.detail_quote: He thought of what she had said after, on the walk — the true thing she had asked him to pretend she hadn't — and did not hand it over. It was hers.

admitted.text: The "chance" meeting reads as calculated, which casts a slight chill over his courtliness.
admitted.detail_quote: He chose it fast and without seeming to, for the angle it gave on the doors and on everyone coming through them.

admitted.text: She reads as the past lover whose privacy Pace violated, a loss that still shapes him.
admitted.detail_quote: Daphne had built a door, once, and he had not respected it.

admitted.text: She reads as a woman who has made her face into armor and has decided to stay behind it, even with Pace.
admitted.detail_quote: She had been perfect, and perfect was safe, and safe had held until a man watched her instead of the face

admitted.text: Being seen and held tenderly seems to frighten her more than any pain.
admitted.detail_quote: Tenderness was something the face received and passed inward, in amounts she decided.

admitted.text: Randi seems unable to admit wanting a woman except by recasting that want as a gift for Pace.
admitted.detail_quote: She had made herself not a woman who hungered for another woman, which he could see was unsurvivable, but a girlfriend offering her man a gift, which was merely sexy.

admitted.text: Her "yes" to Vee reads as plain, helpless desire that got out before the performance could catch it.
admitted.detail_quote: the bare arrival of a thing already true before she got to it.

admitted.text: She reads as a practiced social operator, able to stage a "chance" meeting perfectly.
admitted.detail_quote: A decade of dance and three years of whatever sorority actually taught under the mixers and the letters, all of it folded down into three seconds of execution

admitted.text: Her fidgeting at the coffee shop reads as jealousy or anxiety, not the boredom Vee assumes.
admitted.detail_quote: Twice the cup came up to her mouth and went back down, and no sip happened.

admitted.text: Holding Vee's hand in front of Brooke reads as a real and risky public claim.
admitted.detail_quote: Randi had just spent something on her, in front of the girls who decided what it was worth.

admitted.text: She reads as hungry to belong, dazzled by a world she has only watched from outside.
admitted.detail_quote: she had been chosen, plainly, for reasons she didn't need to understand, by exactly the person she'd have chosen to be chosen by.

admitted.text: She reads as starved in more than one sense, and the meal opens a long-standing emptiness.
admitted.detail_quote: It kept going down and down into something that had been empty a lot longer than since noon.

admitted.text: She seems to police herself in her mother's voice, judging both other girls and her own body.
admitted.detail_quote: The voice said *floozie* in her mother's exact word and her thighs pressed once, hard, on their own

admitted.text: Her feeling for Randi reads as desire she hasn't looked at yet.
admitted.detail_quote: And all Vee could do was look at her with a flat helpless want, the want you keep for a thing you've only ever seen from a distance

admitted.text: She seems to find deep relief in handing over control.
admitted.detail_quote: the relief of handing the choice across the table went through her

admitted.text: She insists on her own agency, and she reads as proud of choosing.
admitted.detail_quote: I did it because I wanted to and I did it on purpose.

admitted.text: She reads as quietly gifted at math and structure, a gift she lets slide when Randi is close.
admitted.detail_quote: the structure under the numbers, the pleasure of the problem opening

admitted.text: She seems to be drifting from Cassie and not letting herself notice.
admitted.detail_quote: And Vee thought, easily, that it was fine to have your own people.

admitted.text: Vee seems naïve about how thoroughly Randi and Pace have arranged the apparent accidents of her new life.
admitted.detail_quote: that she had been chosen, plainly, for reasons she didn't need to understand

admitted.text: She reads as unimpressed by Randi's charm and declines to play along.
admitted.detail_quote: she just put her name down flat in the space, one word, and picked her pencil back up.

admitted.text: She seems loyal and protective, keeping her jokes for Vee rather than for show.
admitted.detail_quote: Cassie never asked — asking was for people who wanted the sad version to get bigger.

admitted.text: She seems quietly hurt at being left behind and hides it.
admitted.detail_quote: whatever had been in them was folded away.

admitted.text: She reads as a velvet-gloved enforcer whose friendliness is a form of surveillance.
admitted.detail_quote: she knew exactly how much authority it took to stay seated while another person stopped walking. Brooke had more of it than she did.

admitted.text: Her friendliness reads as an empty social tool, ready for any use.
admitted.detail_quote: the laugh that meant nothing on its own and was therefore available for anything.

admitted.text: She seems eager to fit in and a little anxious about it.
admitted.detail_quote: Kinsey, who had been waiting for the room to warm to her

admitted.text: The bench hidden as a table: a hidden purpose under an ordinary surface, like the game itself.
admitted.detail_quote: full of what it was, doing what it would continue to do, waiting for the next time.

admitted.text: The thin apple slices: Randi's rationed appetite and Pace's way of feeding it.
admitted.detail_quote: a girl who had been portioning herself, weighing every want before she let herself have it, and who tonight had finally let someone feed her.

admitted.text: The lock and the deadbolt: Randi shutting herself away inside.
admitted.detail_quote: he heard the small click of the lock turning over, which was not a thing she had ever done before in his house.

admitted.text: The mirror smile: the face as a mask laid over the self that begged.
admitted.detail_quote: The face was lying.

admitted.text: The bottle cap pressed into her nail: secret self-punishment after being seen.
admitted.detail_quote: set the sharp inner edge of the cap under her thumbnail and pressed

admitted.text: The single burning maple: Randi's desire turning ahead of everything around it.
admitted.detail_quote: a single tree burning orange in a field of things that had not yet decided to change.

admitted.text: Euler's crossed mark: two things joined at right angles become plain, like a pairing or a triangle.
admitted.detail_quote: Put them together, at right angles, and they turn into a single thing that's suddenly plain — easy to name, easy to know what to do with.

admitted.text: The right-angle mark: reads as Pace and Randi’s planned conjunction, meant to turn Vee’s separate wants into one legible arrangement.
admitted.detail_quote: Put them together, at right angles, and they turn into a single thing that's suddenly plain

admitted.text: The pool: the one place Vee's body belongs to her, untouched by being looked at.
admitted.detail_quote: She had loved this before she had a body to be a problem, and the water was the one part of it that had never been taken.

admitted.text: the cherry pits on wax paper: reads as a lesson in belonging taught without shame, the way Pace teaches everything
admitted.detail_quote: when his own pit came he laid it on the wax paper beside hers

admitted.text: The flannel: Pace's self-sacrifice, kept by Vee as a token of being cared for.
admitted.detail_quote: The flannel was warm on her. It smelled of soap and of a man and of the inside of a gym bag

admitted.text: The moleskin: Pace's quiet, lasting care.
admitted.detail_quote: The square of foam was still on her heel, holding.

admitted.text: What will happen when Vee learns she was picked out for Randi and Pace?
admitted.detail_quote: Randi's *yes* had a name now and a class schedule and a copper head he could still pick out, small, at the far edge of the lawn.

admitted.text: What will Randi decide to do about the self Pace found?
admitted.detail_quote: The one he had found was going back behind it, and she was not coming out again.

admitted.text: What exactly happened with Daphne, and what did it cost Pace?
admitted.detail_quote: it had cost him more than he had known, then, that anything could cost.

admitted.text: Is Pace's growing care for Vee drifting beyond the game he and Randi agreed on?
admitted.detail_quote: He looked at you like he'd forgotten there was anyone else in the room

admitted.text: Is Pace rich, given his built furniture and cheap counters?
admitted.detail_quote: broken by one thin pale line where nothing grew.

admitted.text: What did Cassie see that made her say a final-sounding goodbye?
admitted.detail_quote: It landed a little wrong. *Goodbye* — not *see you later,* not *text me,* not *bye* — the whole word, flat and finished

admitted.text: Will Vee's friendship with Cassie survive Randi pulling her away?
admitted.detail_quote: Underneath it something turned over, small, and she let it lie

admitted.text: Will Pace act on the russet dress Vee said she couldn't afford?
admitted.detail_quote: There's a black dress in the back of my closet. It's been good enough for every dinner I've had to dress for.

admitted.text: What was Vee about to say to Pace before the siren cut her off?
admitted.detail_quote: The thing she wanted to say was bigger than any words she had for it

admitted.text: How far do Randi and Pace intend to carry their private plan for Vee?
admitted.detail_quote: I already do," Randi said, and it came out easy and bright
